records.legacyMechanics: Athletic-width standing, ribs over pelvis, ball at chest, light brace/exhale, fast horizontal pass to wall/partner/open target, then safe catch or retrieval and full reset. The legacy card mixes return possibilities and does not fix exact ball mass/size/distance or permitted preload.

records.name: Stationary Bilateral Chest Projection to Contained Target — instructional adaptation
records.sourceRelationship: Preserves bilateral forward chest projection and controlled throw-only reset, but intentionally changes exact wall/preload/intent/target/return context. No completed exact stationary/no-preload/open-contained-target profile was verified.

exactProposedMechanics.start: Stationary bilateral athletic-width stance with knees comfortably unlocked, ribs/pelvis organized, one individually fitting ball at chest held by both hands.
exactProposedMechanics.preload: No deliberate squat/dip, step, jump or rotational wind-up. If these appear, record the actual deviation rather than silently renaming the source.
exactProposedMechanics.release: On the single already explained release cue, project the ball forward from chest height with both hands and controlled arm extension toward the declared open contained target area; retain foot contacts and balanced finish.
exactProposedMechanics.target: Measured inspected open release lane with a contained area for the ball's natural landing after forward chest-height projection; do not aim or drive the ball downward as a slam. Ball and surface must fit the declared dead or low-bounce behavior. No wall rebound, partner catch or airborne catch is prescribed.
exactProposedMechanics.afterRelease: Keep position and wait. No chasing, catching, rebound exchange or immediate extra throw.
exactProposedMechanics.retrieval: Collect only after the globally declared all-clear, all releases have stopped, balls are settled and the coach has confirmed the entire retrieval area/route is clear. Follow the exact walking pickup/carry/return path; no throws while any person retrieves.
exactProposedMechanics.reset: Return to the declared ready/waiting area and safely reestablish the ball-at-chest start only as instructed. Root must state who handles pickup/return when athlete handling is not established.

readinessForAuthoredTask: Independently comfortable stationary stance and unloaded bilateral forward arm action.

Can securely hold the ACTUAL ball at chest and comfortably control the actual floor pickup, short carry and floor set-down used for own-ball retrieval, observed in counted P2 instruction or a direct equivalent. Rack holding alone does not establish floor retrieval.

No prior successful throw is required for the first counted E1 instructional release. Entry requires comfortable actual handling/chest start and unloaded arm path, understood conduct, and verified equipment/space; controlled release, stable feet and organized torso are observed during that first counted E1 attempt.
Understands the one release cue, no-catch/no-chase/wait rules, global all-clear and actual retrieval role.
Inspected contained lane/target/ball behavior, surface, supervision and total throw/upper-body budget fit.
records.prerequisiteInterpretation: Entry to the first counted E1 instructional release requires comfortable actual ball handling/chest start and own-retrieval floor pickup/carry/set-down, comfortable unloaded arm path, understood release/wait/retrieval conduct and verified equipment/space. Actual controlled release is observed within E1, not demanded as a prior successful throw. P2 has no release and cannot grant a throwing or full throw/retrieval conduct pass. Its floor-handling observation or a direct equivalent supplies the physical retrieval prerequisite; a rack-only hold does not. The task does not inherit an unused countermovement/squat prerequisite, and an old front-support-shape name alone does not establish handling.

ballSelectionBoundary.rule: Root must assign the actual inspected ball's type, mass, diameter, texture/grip and bounce behavior. Comfortable handling is observed in counted P2 instruction or a direct equivalent before the first E1 release; actual release control is observed within counted E1. No prior successful throw or universal age mass/size was verified.
ballSelectionBoundary.deadLowBounce: Dead/low-bounce is a declared implement/target choice that must fit the actual surface and containment. A slam ball is not automatically interchangeable with a medicine ball; ball design, size, grip and release suitability must be verified.
ballSelectionBoundary.unexpectedBounce: Stop for uncontained/unexpected bounce or roll; do not retrieve until global clearance is restored.

cueContext.knownCue: One early explained cue maps to one already specified chest projection. No catch, choice target, surprise rule or perceptual complexity is implied.
cueContext.competencyBoundary: Following a known release permission cue supports an observed task-specific instruction/cue result only. It does not by itself establish reaction speed, unpredictable choice or reactive catching.
cueContext.globalAllClear: Explicit authored group-control rule informed by source lane shutdown, not a copied exact programming-method profile.

records.exposureAccounting: Count every actual ball release, including unsuccessful qualification/invalid attempts. Zero intentional athlete flight/landing events when both feet stay grounded; ball release/landing and any handling are separate exposures. Do not substitute valid-throw quotas for bounded attempts.
stopRules: Stop for symptoms, apprehension, unsafe ball/target/traffic, failed grip, unplanned step/jump/dip, torso extension, loss of balance or uncontrolled release.
Stop for unexpected bounce/roll, target containment failure, premature retrieval or cue misunderstanding.
Do not add repeated attempts to earn a throwing pass; use an independently eligible no-throw branch when handling/release is unavailable.
remainingGates: Root must supply actual ball mass/diameter/fit, release distance/target dimensions, intended effort, bounded attempts, recovery and full global-clear/retrieval clock.
Exact stationary/open-target/release-cue identity/profile and current approval remain unset pending review.
Verify separate actual throwing and cue observations before any JUMP-T/REACT-T mapping; neither is earned by no-throw rehearsal or attendance.

records.name: Unloaded Bilateral Forward Reach and Return — orientation teaching task
records.sourceRelationship: The loaded chest-pass sequence supplies related start/arm-path context only. No completed exact unloaded standing bilateral reach/retract profile was verified; this is newly authored documentation, not a scapular rehabilitation or loaded pressing exercise.
records.exactProposedMechanics: From independently comfortable quiet bilateral standing, bring empty hands to the declared comfortable chest-height start; reach both hands forward through a comfortable range without stepping, dipping, shrugging or rib flare; return hands to the start and relax. Root supplies actual hand orientation, range, cadence, repetitions and cues. No ball or release is present.
prerequisites: Comfortable standing and the actual unloaded shoulder/elbow/wrist motion.
Understands the small reach/return and stop instruction; no symptoms or forced range.
records.competencyBoundary: Unloaded arm-path/position observation only. No ball handling, throwing, chest-pass power, retrieval or reaction-performance pass.
stopRules: Stop for symptoms, discomfort, balance/trunk change or forced arm range.
If unloaded arm motion is unavailable but quiet standing is independently comfortable, use the separate BILATERAL-STAND-TEACH record; otherwise defer.
remainingGates: Root must fully prescribe actual range, arms/hands, repetitions, cadence, return and clock.
No exact canonical/profile ID is invented for this nonthrow task.

rootProposedP1Context.boundary: Forty seconds includes root-authored explanation, demonstration, brief unloaded reach/return actions and resets; it is not a40-second sustained reach or an exact source dose.

records.name: Ball-at-Chest Hold with Declared Handling — floor-handling instruction or rack-hold practice
records.exactProposedMechanics: P2 is one separately segmented no-release floor-handling instruction: controlled floor pickup to chest over 5 s; comfortable stationary chest hold 5 s; short 1 m out-and-back carry over 4 s (2 s walking plus 2 s turning); controlled floor set-down 6 s; exit/reset 4 s. Restore the ball to the same start between groups. Observe actual comfort in this counted action after plausible equipment selection and demonstration; stop and manage set-down immediately if unsuitable. E1 no-release practice is a different shorter rack pickup 2 s / chest hold 3 s / rack set-down 3 s / reset 2 s task. During each chest hold feet are stationary; P2 explicitly includes floor lowering, walking and turning in its handling phases. Neither context includes release, push-out, catch, throwing preload or jumping.
prerequisites: P2 instructional entry: comfortable standing, ordinary walking/turning and unloaded chest-start arm position; inspected plausible implement selected for this athlete using actual size/load/grip and available prior information; exact floor pickup/carry/set-down demonstrated. Comfortable unloaded floor access must be independently known or observed during the initial reach of the same counted P2 pickup before taking the ball load. A partial-range hinge is not a floor-access pass.
Understands the hold/wait/set-down and stop instructions, can communicate discomfort, and has direct supervision with a way to end the action safely; no toss/catch handoff is assumed.

E1 no-release rack practice entry: actual comfortable grip and chest hold from P2 or a direct equivalent, plus an independently appropriate rack height, access and handling arrangement. P2 observes floor return, not rack return; the first scheduled E1 rack action observes actual rack pickup/set-down with no extra trial. E1 throw with own retrieval additionally requires actual comfortable floor pickup/carry/set-down from P2 or a direct equivalent; rack-only comfort is insufficient. Unfamiliar grip/holding is not automatically eligible for the shorter E1 practice envelope.
records.eligibilityBoundary: No prior successful loaded ball hold or floor-retrieval trial is required for the first counted P2 instructional action when its instruction-entry conditions are met. If comfortable unloaded floor access is not established, observe the initial reach within the same counted pickup before taking load; an unsuitable reach ends that action before lifting and the coach manages the ball. Do not add a screening repetition. P2 supplies actual fit and physical floor-handling/carry observations; unsuitable grip, load, position, lowering, carrying or return ends the action with coach-managed set-down, partial exposure recorded and no extra trial. E1 no-release rack practice requires its actual comfortable handling; E1 throw with own retrieval requires actual comfortable floor pickup/carry/set-down and chest handling. If the relevant evidence is unavailable, use an independently eligible unloaded/quiet-standing E1 route; unknown handling does not earn a passed no-release or retrieval fallback.
records.competencyBoundary: Record actual chest start/hold, floor pickup, 2 m loaded carry with turn and floor set-down separately for P2; shorter E1 rack practice supplies only its actual rack/static handling observations. Neither supplies release, throwing, cue-reactivity, catching or JUMP-T/REACT-T pass. Floor handling is a physical retrieval prerequisite; the full global all-clear/own-ball retrieval sequence is observed during counted E1.
remainingGates: Root must state actual ball identity/load/size, hold time, pickup/handoff/return, supervision and clock.
No completed exact standalone ball-start-hold profile was verified; canonical IDs remain null.

rootProposedP2Context.task: One counted coached floor pickup to chest, brief chest hold, short carry/turn and floor set-down; actual comfortable handling may be established here after plausible inspected implement selection and demonstration. No prior successful loaded trial and no release is demanded.
rootProposedP2Context.boundary: The 140-second envelope includes explanation/demonstration, brief individual holds, handling and reset. It is not a 140-second continuous loaded hold and includes no throw, catch or hidden release. End unsuitable handling immediately and record the actual partial exposure; no extra ball trial or throwing pass is awarded. Subsequent work uses an independently eligible unloaded/quiet-standing branch when comfortable handling remains unestablished.
rootProposedP2Context.ballStart: Same inspected floor location between groups; no rack-only substitution silently establishes floor retrieval.
rootProposedP2Context.accounting: One actual floor pickup, one 5 s chest hold, 2 m loaded carry with turn, one floor set-down, zero releases. Record partial completion separately; no extra fit trial.
rootProposedP2Context.E1NoReleasePractice: Rack pickup 2 s, hold 3 s, rack set-down 3 s, reset 2 s = 10 s; actual rack fit/handling required and no floor retrieval pass inferred.

defaultUnknownHandlingBranch.onlyWhen: Unloaded movement and standing are independently comfortable. This is the main-practice route when actual comfortable handling remains unestablished; it does not prohibit the separately gated first counted P2 handling instruction.
defaultUnknownHandlingBranch.boundary: No throwing, ball handling or release competence is inferred. If standing itself is unavailable, defer rather than forcing a movement fallback.
